data.narrative:
Morpheus Space is a Series A–stage space and aerospace company founded by Daniel Bock and István Lőrincz that has raised $43M+ to date. The valuation exercise draws from a universe of 13 comparable companies: 5 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private firms including SpaceX, Sierra Space, Planet Labs, Impulse Space, and Apex Space.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($43M) as a baseline proxy for early-stage valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $86M. This method reflects the pattern that Series A investors typically expect 2x value creation before the next financing event.

Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied due to lack of target revenue disclosure; the Space & Aerospace sector median P/S ratio stands at 23.9x across six public tickers, but without Morpheus's revenue, translation to absolute valuation is not possible. Peer-median analysis is similarly inapplicable—while 11 same-sector private comparables exist, no subset of three or more truly parallel-stage, similar-tier firms is available for statistical confidence.

The single-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $73M to $99M, centered on $86M. Primary uncertainties include revenue trajectory, near-term capital requirements, and relative competitive positioning within an increasingly crowded launch-services and space-infrastructure landscape.
